formal_acceptance_note: Data structures, UI, persistence, and all five Evidence regions are fully implemented and verified for every Alpha. Only A101 currently has Product-Owner-approved (source=John, version=v0.1) invalidation content; every other Alpha honestly reports approval_status=not_defined with an empty conditions list -- this is expected, not a defect, per the task's own explicit instruction not to fabricate unapproved content.

audit_findings_before_implementation.bull_evidence_bear_evidence_current_sema: Raw, unfiltered, non-deduplicated per-claim lists (built at API read time by routes_research._attach_conflict_evidence, joined from bull_structure/bear_structure's claim_ids against persisted alpha_matches rows) -- included ANY qualifying claim regardless of B1 stance (opposes_alpha/mentions_alpha/neutral_background all leaked through), never deduplicated into Evidence Facts. This is the exact stale/incorrect behavior task section 4 required B5 to fix.
audit_findings_before_implementation.b2_evidence_pool_location: conflict_admissibility.evaluate_conflict_admissibility already stance-filters (supports_alpha only) and fact-groups (via conflict_detector._group_qualifying_claims_into_facts) each side, but only exposed counts/IDs (SideAdmissibility), never the full fact objects needed for display -- B5 reuses the same stance-filtering/grouping functions directly rather than re-deriving them.
audit_findings_before_implementation.b1_final_stance_storage: candidate_scores[].evidence_stance on each alpha_matches.json record, written by structure_engine.alpha_mapper._attach_evidence_stance / evidence_stance_llm.apply_llm_stance_upgrade -- read via the same stance_for_alpha pool-search pattern conflict_admissibility.py already uses.
audit_findings_before_implementation.counter_alpha_id_storage: candidate_scores[].counter_alpha_id, present only when evidence_stance == supports_counter_alpha -- confirmed present in real saved-run data.
audit_findings_before_implementation.persistence_whitelist_risk_confirmed: week4_persistence._whitelist_conflict/_whitelist_candidate use narrow, explicit reconstruction (not raw pass-through) -- a new field added to the payload without an explicit whitelist entry is silently dropped on persistence, exactly the same risk class as prior B3/B4 findings.
audit_findings_before_implementation.conflict_api_read_path: get_persisted_conflicts spreads the full DB-reconstructed result ({**result, status: 'ok'}) -- safe once persistence carries the field; no separate narrow reconstruction at this layer.
audit_findings_before_implementation.frontend_current_display: ConflictRadarPage showed only a Main Conflict card, an admitted-conflicts list, and bare arbitration COUNTS -- candidate/suppressed/rejected pairs were never individually rendered at all before this task.
audit_findings_before_implementation.candidate_conflict_api_exposure: arbitration.candidate_evaluations[] (with each pair's own admissibility detail) already flowed through the Conflicts API, but the frontend TypeScript type never declared admissibility and the UI never rendered these items -- additive wiring only, no new backend computation needed for this part.
audit_findings_before_implementation.taxonomy_invalidation_conditions_found: alpha_taxonomy_v1.yaml already has a per-Alpha invalidation_conditions field (including for A101: ['AI capex cuts', 'model demand slows', 'GPU oversupply']) -- differently worded from John's freshly-supplied text and carrying no source/version/approval_status metadata. Treated as NOT a formal approval source (see section on invalidation below) -- never read or modified by B5.

bull_evidence_contract.deduplication: unique Evidence Fact groups (reuses evidence_fact_index.group_evidence_candidates via conflict_detector._group_qualifying_claims_into_facts verbatim -- never raw claim counts

counter_evidence_routing.case_a_opposes_alpha: a claim whose stance relative to a conflict side's own alpha_id is opposes_alpha becomes Counter Evidence against that alpha
counter_evidence_routing.case_b_supports_counter_alpha: a claim with evidence_stance=supports_counter_alpha and counter_alpha_id equal to the conflict's OTHER side becomes Counter Evidence against the side it was evaluated relative to, tagged supports_counter_alpha_id
excludes: an unrelated counter_alpha_id not matching the conflict's other side
counter_evidence_routing.dual_role_preserved: the same underlying claim can appear in bear_evidence (supports_alpha relative to its own matched_alpha) AND in counter_evidence (opposes_alpha/supports_counter_alpha relative to a different alpha it also carries a candidate_scores entry for) -- both roles kept independently, never dropped
counter_evidence_routing.real_data_confirmation: the real saved NVDA run's PEG rebuttal claim (see section 'real_saved_run' below) exhibits exactly this dual role and is displayed correctly in both places
counter_evidence_routing.search_scope_design_decision: searches the UNION of bull_qualifying and bear_qualifying (both already B2-quality-gated pools for this specific conflict pair) rather than either side alone or the run's full unrelated alpha_matches pool -- required because a claim's matched_alpha (which scopes bull_qualifying/bear_qualifying membership) can differ from an alpha it also carries a stance verdict for in its own candidate_scores list; found and fixed via a failing synthetic test before this ever reached the real-run verification, which then independently confirmed the same scenario occurs in real production data

missing_evidence_calculation.source: conflict_admissibility.AdmissibilityResult (SideAdmissibility per side) -- already-computed B2 counts, never re-derived

reasons.NO_ADMISSIBLE_SUPPORTING_POLARITY: additive diagnosis: side has qualifying evidence of some polarity but zero supports_alpha -- never replaces INSUFFICIENT_SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE, only supplements it

missing_evidence_calculation.admitted_conflict_result: always [] -- falls out naturally from B2's own ADMITTED requiring zero reason_codes on both sides, no special-casing needed
missing_evidence_calculation.score_gap_separation: ALPHA_SCORE_BELOW_THRESHOLD lives in qualification_gaps, never missing_evidence, per task section 7's explicit instruction

invalidation_source_coverage.reasoning: alpha_taxonomy_v1.yaml's own invalidation_conditions field for A101 (['AI capex cuts', 'model demand slows', 'GPU oversupply']) predates this task, carries no source/version/approval_status metadata, and differs in wording from John's freshly-supplied text -- if it had been the formally-approved source, John would not have needed to re-supply a fresh, differently-worded, explicitly-attributed version for this task. Never read, modified, or upgraded to 'approved' status.
invalidation_source_coverage.non_authoritative_draft_proposals: The taxonomy's own existing invalidation_conditions field (for every Alpha) is a plausible future starting point for formal Product Owner review, but is NOT included in the production registry and NOT presented as approved anywhere in this implementation.
